full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiff is that the disputed land originally belonged to Radha Mohan Saha who enjoyed the land through the tenants except plot No. 337. Subsequently, the said Radha Mohan Saha regained the possession of the same entire suit land from the tenants. Thereafter, the plaintiff's predecessor took pattan by Hukumnama dated 25th March, 1354 from the grandson of Radha Mohan Saha and thereafter the plaintiff is enjoying and possessing the said suit land by paying rent to the superior landlord. During revision settlement the same land was wrongly recorded in the name of Government. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed an application before the settlement officer for correction of the said record, which was rejected. Thereafter the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.21 of 1973 for correction of record and obtained ex parte decree on 25-7-1973. He also filed another suit for permanent injunction being No.l1O of 1975 impleading the defendant-petitioners and also obtained ex parte decree. The defendants filed Title Suit No.151 of 1975 for declaration that the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.21 of 1973 is illegal and void and the suit was also decreed 12-4-1977. Thereafter the defendant No.4 threatened to evict them from the suit land and hence the instant suit for declaration of title. 

 While adjudicating the appeal, the appellate Court below came to a conclusion that the plaintiff proved his case beyond any reasonable doubt by adducing both oral and documentary evidence and the case is not barred by limitation or res judicata. Further, the lower appellate Court found that the defendants failed to adduce any evidence in support of their claim except SA and RS records though the defendants claimed their possession in the suit land as well as claimed that the suit property is a channel. It appears that Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1973 was preferred by the plaintiff for correction of certain records resulting ex parte decree though the said decree was set aside in Title Suit No.151 of 1975 preferred by the defendants-petitioners. But in Title Suit No. 110 of 1975 the plaintiff obtained decree of permanent injunction, which still stands valid. The plaintiff in the instant case claimed right and title by way of pattas conveyed through the Hukumnama executed in Bangla year 1334 which is marked as Exhibit I in the trial Court and also the plaintiff adduced certain dakhilas regarding payment of rent to the superior landlord. On perusal of the said Exhibit I it appears that the said pattan was executed followed by delivery of possession and it is of 1354 BS and the said documents were exhibited and considered as evidence by the trial Court though the defendant-petitioner raised objection but failed to prove the same as forged. The trial Court further observed that the said documents are forged and manufactured i.e. written later with new ink. But as it appears that the same documents were produced in the year 1973 in the Court of law in Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 1973. It further appears that both PWs 2 and 3 categorically proved the documents as well as the exclusive possession of the plaintiff but the trial Court miserably failed to discuss these important aspects of law.
